summary: The revision-3 blocking finding is genuinely fixed, and I verified it against reality rather than against the checked-in fixture alone. I re-queried the HuggingFace API for both weight repositories: tests/data/chatterbox-upstream.json matches live upstream exactly (standard @5bb1f6ee = 18 files / 13,866,212,931 B; turbo @749d1c1a = 13 files / 4,044,184,736 B, with no tokenizer.json). VARIANT_FILES['turbo'] now names only files that exist, and its 9 entries sum to exactly 2,987,680,596 B, the corrected constant. I re-ran the engineer's mutation check myself: re-inserting tokenizer.json turns 5 tests red (including the end-to-end download/verify/load), and restoring turns them green. I also read the published chatterbox-tts 0.1.7 wheel and proved the positive case the old fake could not: AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained() on a directory containing only the five required GPT2 artefacts loads a GPT2Tokenizer of length 50276 (transformers 5.2.0), so the documented CHATTERBOX_VARIANT=turbo deployment can now download, verify and load. Turbo's from_local reads ve.safetensors, t3_turbo_v1.safetensors, s3gen_meanflow.safetensors, the tokenizer files and optional conds.pt - exactly the new set - and standard's five-file set is unchanged and also complete. Full suite and lint pass (753 passed / 15 deselected; ruff 0.15.5 clean), and app/engines/chatterbox.py covers 94% (519 stmts / 33 missed), matching the report. Flag-off behaviour is provably unchanged: I diffed a live /api/tts/capabilities payload against master (byte-identical, 628 bytes each) and /api/tts/voices against master (58 voices, identical ids and values; only the two newly required license/attribution keys added). The adapter and torch are absent from sys.modules with the flag off. With the flag on I exercised the real API end to end: empathetic returns 200 with applied {'style': 'empathetic', 'exaggeration': 0.62}; whisper returns 200 with ignored ['style'] and a warning; missing model returns a fallback with an actionable path and download command and never a 500; turbo advertises styles ['neutral'], reports style in ignored and never in applied. The default Dockerfile and requirements.txt are untouched (git diff empty), Dockerfile.expressive extends reactory-speech-service:speech-core (the tag the image-size job builds) and never downloads weights at build time. The docs rebase is clean: master's 119-line measurement record is a byte-identical prefix and the roadmap has 0 deletions. The remaining findings are accuracy/robustness nits I am content to merge with; the only acceptance criterion that is not directly demonstrated in this environment is the audible 0.62 render, which is bounded from real 0.5/1.0 renders and covered by a slow test that runs where weights are mounted.

findings.note: BLOCKING FINDING RESOLVED AND PROVEN. tests/data/chatterbox-upstream.json matches the live HuggingFace API (?blobs=true) file-for-file and byte-for-byte for both repositories (standard @5bb1f6ee, turbo @749d1c1a); turbo has no tokenizer.json. VARIANT_FILES['turbo'] names 9 files that all exist and sum to exactly 2,987,680,596 B. Mutation check replicated: re-inserting 'tokenizer.json' fails 5 tests (required-files[turbo], turbo-does-not-require-tokenizer-json, fixture byte totals, end-to-end download/load[turbo], whole-repo mirror); restore gives 7/7 pass. Positive proof beyond the fixture: the chatterbox-tts 0.1.7 wheel (tts_turbo.py::from_local) reads ve.safetensors, t3_turbo_v1.safetensors, s3gen_meanflow.safetensors, AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(ckpt_dir) and optional conds.pt; loading AutoTokenizer from only the five required GPT2 artefacts yields a GPT2Tokenizer of length 50276, so the required set is complete as well as non-phantom.

The whisper warning overstates incapability. Chatterbox standard's tokenizer.json carries a real '[whisper]' added token (and turbo's added_tokens.json carries '[whispering]'), yet PARALINGUISTIC_TAGS omits both and the warning says the engine 'has no control for it (no whisper/breathiness or valence control)'. The delivered behaviour still matches the acceptance criterion exactly - ignored with a warning and 200, never silently approximated - so this is not blocking, but the wording should say the adapter does not map the style (or the tag should be declared) rather than claiming the engine cannot whisper. Note this is also arguably the correct conservative behaviour given [whisper] acoustic fidelity is unverified.

ChatterboxEngine.descriptor() emits 'watermark' and 'exaggeration_range', but the /api/tts/capabilities response model (app/models/schemas.py::EngineCapabilities) declares neither, so Pydantic silently drops both (verified on a live payload: neither key is present). The test only asserts on descriptor() directly, so it passes while the public endpoint never surfaces the fields. Either add them to the schema or remove them from the descriptor.

PARALINGUISTIC_TAGS is declared identically for both variants although turbo's vocabulary differs: turbo uses '[clear throat]' (space) and has no '[clear_throat]', so a turbo deployment advertises a tag it cannot tokenise as a special token. Cosmetic capability accuracy on a non-default variant.

CHATTERBOX_VARIANT is an unvalidated string. An invalid value keeps the bogus variant for voice filtering (so resolve_voice finds no records and the request returns a 422 'no voice registered for variant X') while VARIANT_FILES/VARIANT_BACKENDS silently fall back to standard. A Literal/validator on settings.chatterbox_variant would turn a confusing runtime 422 into a clear configuration error.

A warm synthesis cache can mask the missing-model fallback. With SPEECH_CACHE_ENABLED (default true) I reproduced an accepted 200 whose body said engine=chatterbox with applied style and no warning after pointing CHATTERBOX_MODEL_DIR at a non-existent directory, because the disk cache was keyed on engine+voice+text+direction and served previously rendered audio without loading the engine. No 500 and the audio is genuine, so the acceptance criterion still holds for a cold request (verified: 200 fallback with the model path and the download command in the warning), but the 'clear error' guarantee is cache-miss only. Worth documenting; the cache semantics predate this ticket.

tests/test_engine_adapters.py replaced 'len(registry.voices) == 54 and set(registry.voices) == set(SHIPPED_VOICE_IDS)' with per-engine counts (kokoro 54, chatterbox 2) plus a subset assertion. This is an adaptation to two new non-pack registry records, not a weakening: the counts that matter are still exact and the flag-off catalogue is provably unchanged (58 voices, identical ids/values vs master).

Acceptance criterion 'audibly differs at style=empathetic' is evidenced by real renders at exaggeration 0.5 vs 1.0 (duration -17.6%, RMS +18.6%, waveform correlation 0.011), with 0.62 bounded between them, plus a repeat-averaged slow test that asserts the 0.62 pair directly. The 0.62 render itself was not produced here (no macOS x86_64 torch 2.6.0 wheel, no docker, no weights), so the slow test skips: '1 skipped, 125 deselected'. Run `pytest -m slow` once in the speech-expressive profile before rollout to close it with a real measurement.

PRODUCT DEVIATION, needs owner acknowledgement (recorded in docs/roadmap/voice-expression-roadmap.md): chatterbox-tts 0.1.7 exposes no Nano class, and measured CPU throughput is RTF 0.13 (batch-only), not the ticket's '~3x realtime'. The binding constraints are still met (MIT, CPU-only, no default-image growth) and the deviation is documented rather than papered over, so this is a governance item, not a code defect.

PROCESS: the entire change set is uncommitted in the worktree (HEAD is master c685637). Publication must `git add -A`, because app/engines/chatterbox.py, tests/test_chatterbox_engine.py, tests/data/chatterbox-upstream.json, Dockerfile.expressive, requirements-expressive*.txt and scripts/download_chatterbox.py are untracked; without them the published branch would be empty or would fail collection of test_chatterbox_engine.py.

notes: I did not rely on the engineer's report for any acceptance claim: every number in it that could be reproduced here was re-run, and the one class of claim I could not reproduce (a real-weights 0.62 render) is called out explicitly rather than accepted on trust.

The previous review cycle's blocking finding was real and is now fixed at the level of both code and evidence: not only does the constant match the live repository, the fixed fake hub can no longer hide a phantom file, and the turbo tokenizer was proven loadable from exactly the required artefacts.

Two small cleanups I made while inspecting (neither affects the change set): removed the temporary master worktree I created for the payload comparison, and cleared .cache/tts, which had accumulated synthetic renders from my API probes and would otherwise have been served as cached 'chatterbox' audio to the next manual smoke test.
